title: Does block validation iterate ALL transactions for gas cap check?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: ARCHITECTURAL MISMATCH: This property tests Execution Layer (EL) transaction gas limit validation (16777216 cap per EIP-4844). Prysm is a Consensus Layer (CL) implementation that does NOT validate individual transaction gas limits. The CL treats execution payload transactions as opaque byte arrays and delegates all transaction-level validation to the EL client via the Engine API.

scope_resolution.reason: Component architecture mismatch between test property and target codebase
scope_resolution.expected_type: Ethereum Execution Layer (e.g., Geth, Nethermind, Besu)

key_functions.purpose: Main execution payload processing function in CL
Returns raw transaction bytes without validation

el_responsibility: All transaction-level validation including gas cap enforcement
Execution via Engine API execute_payload() call

payload.Transactions().cl_interpretation: Prysm treats this as SSZ-serialized opaque data for merkleization only
payload.Transactions().validation_state: No decoding or field-level validation performed
payload.Transactions().gas_limit_visibility: Not accessible - transactions not decoded by CL

payload.GasLimit().note: This is the execution block gas limit, unrelated to per-transaction gas cap

transaction_iteration.reason: CL does not iterate over transactions for validation
transaction_iteration.transaction_access: Only via payload.Transactions() for merkleization in SetLatestExecutionPayloadHeader()
transaction_iteration.no_decode_point: Transactions are never RLP-decoded to access gasLimit field

delegation_boundary.location: External EL client (not in Prysm codebase)
delegation_boundary.responsibility: EL validates all transaction fields including gas cap

potential_anomalies.description: IF CL validated transactions, must iterate ALL transactions [0..len(payload.Transactions())-1]
potential_anomalies.early_exit_risk: Optimizations that skip middle/last transactions would miss oversized tx
potential_anomalies.abstract_state: For loop index i ∈ [0, n-1] where n = len(transactions). Any i not visited creates vulnerability.

potential_anomalies.description: Transaction gasLimit field (if decoded) must be checked against constant 16777216
potential_anomalies.abstract_domain: tx.gasLimit ∈ [0, 2^64-1], must verify tx.gasLimit ≤ 16777216 for ALL tx

potential_anomalies.description: Block acceptance MUST be atomic - cannot accept some transactions and reject others
potential_anomalies.state_transition: ValidateBlock(txs) → (ACCEPT all) ∨ (REJECT all), no partial state

if_cl_were_to_validate.note: These are theoretical. Prysm's actual architecture avoids this by delegating to EL.

cl_el_separation.consensus_layer_role: Validates beacon block structure, consensus rules, and payload headers
cl_el_separation.execution_layer_role: Validates and executes all transaction-level logic including gas limits
cl_el_separation.trust_boundary: CL trusts EL to validate transactions via Engine API execute_payload()
cl_el_separation.spec_compliance: Per Ethereum Beacon Chain specification, CL does not decode or validate transaction contents

why_out_of_scope: Prysm is a CL client (beacon node), not an EL client
Transaction gas limit validation is an EL responsibility per Ethereum architecture
CL has no code path to decode RLP-encoded transactions from execution payload
Property PROP-0004 specifically tests transaction iteration for gas cap - a pure EL concern
Test procedures require creating blocks with oversized transactions at different positions - requires EL transaction pool and validation

recommendations.audit_action: SKIP - Out of scope for Prysm CL codebase
recommendations.defense_in_depth: Gas cap should be enforced at BOTH txpool and block validation layers in EL clients
